headline: High-risk default interaction: slim’s broad filesystem/network actions can cascade from ai-engineering-hub outputs, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the pair’s lack of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented between ai-engineering-hub and slim, so direct injection is not default. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or operator-mediated transfer into slim’s interactive CLI prompt, which is a small blast radius but still possible.
conditions: IF the operator manually pastes ai-engineering-hub output into slim’s CLI prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added later, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Avoid pasting untrusted text into slim prompts.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from upstream output.
Review any copied content before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.
requires-engineering: add a parser that rejects instruction-like text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is documented with no data classes touched and no network egress, while slim touches filesystem artifacts and registry credentials but has no documented shared workspace with agent_a. Without a shared channel, leakage between them is not a default pathway; the main risk is operator-mediated transfer of sensitive files into slim.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, leakage risk increases.
IF registry credentials or private keys are copied from slim outputs into ai-engineering-hub prompts, they may be exposed in downstream text.
mitigations: Keep separate working directories.
Do not paste secrets from slim into ai-engineering-hub.
Redact credentials before sharing outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning on handoff artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ai-engineering-hub shows no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for slim’s mutable resources by default. slim can write files and execute shells, but modify_git_state is false and no shared writable target is documented, making direct capability conflict unlikely unless the operator maps both to the same directory.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF the operator runs slim inside a repo that ai-engineering-hub also edits, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use distinct output directories.
Run slim on copies, not source trees.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration locking.
requires-engineering: mount read-only inputs for ai-engineering-hub.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A plausible cascade exists if ai-engineering-hub produces recommendations or generated text that slim’s operator treats as authoritative during container/image processing. slim has interactive CLI command execution and broad filesystem/network access, so a mistaken upstream instruction can propagate into real actions even though no direct automation link is documented.
conditions: IF slim’s operator follows ai-engineering-hub output without verification, errors can cascade into executed commands.
IF ai-engineering-hub emits malformed or stale guidance, slim may act on it during image analysis.
mitigations: Require a human verification step before executing suggested commands.
Cross-check any generated instructions against source docs.
Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs advisory only.
requires-engineering: add structured, machine-checked handoff formats.
requires-engineering: add approval gates before shell execution.

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, while ai-engineering-hub has no documented compliance controls or data residency guarantees. If sensitive artifacts from slim are routed into ai-engineering-hub’s documentation or prompts, retention and residency obligations may be breached; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF certificate private keys or registry credentials are copied from slim into ai-engineering-hub artifacts, compliance exposure increases.
IF the operator stores slim outputs in a shared documentation system, retention policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared notes.
Redact keys and credentials before transfer.
Keep compliance-sensitive artifacts in a restricted vault.
requires-engineering: document retention and residency rules for both tools.
requires-engineering: segregate regulated data from general documentation.
